title: Dizzy series discovery: source, ports and reconstruction evidence
summary: Review 24 Dizzy-related roots: add ten source/reconstruction projects; hold or exclude fourteen insufficient, derivative or unrelated candidates.
notes: Root personally searched the Dizzy series, individual titles, source/disassembly/remake terms, language-specific repositories and linked authors. Reviewed 24 pinned repository roots: ten additions and fourteen held/excluded candidates. No worker performed discovery. Existing catalogue contains the unrelated madmoose DOS disassembler and Mushroom Pie engine; neither is duplicated. Treasure Island remake is explicitly distinguished from original-algorithm recovery; the stronger Fantasy World ports and Magicland disassembly retain edition, timing, build and fidelity limitations. No upstream code was executed. Separately fetched HEAD commits match pinned tree references. Cached proof texts are included only when their Git blob hashes match; large or encoding-converted sources remain linked rather than presented as byte-verified cached proofs. Dr. Titus describes independently disassembling Treasure Island in a primary-author forum post, but a public source deliverable was not established in this pass; do not turn that anecdote into a source-reconstruction repository entry. This is a broad series-focused pass, not a claim of exhaustive discovery.

sources.reason: Documented NDX/RES chunk indexes and variable-bit dictionary decompression, unpack/repack scripts, sprite and layered-stage viewers. This is original game resource analysis, not a reconstructed playable engine.

Game-specific code/data declarations identify map records, function indexes, sprite masks and named drawing operations. Generated and refactored assembly retain generic addresses and unknown regions, so semantic analysis is incomplete.

Contains Oliver Twins PDS-era Z80 source with Spectrum/CPC build choices, native 6502 BBC gameplay, and a separately unfinished C64 cartridge disassembly. Main loop, inventory and actor routines are translated into host assembly rather than a Z80 interpreter.

Annotated MACRO-11-style reconstruction of the 1994 MBS/TD adaptation, with room, sprite, bank-switching, collision and Russian dialogue analysis. Despite the name Dizzy 1, this is a reworking of Fantasy World Dizzy.

Semantic port of the 2023 Russian extended 128K version. Named collision and inventory functions identify original addresses; original-derived 12.5 Hz integer logic is tested against captured traces. Rendering interpolation, stable inventory slots, saves and remaster colouring are intentional changes.

Substantial game recreation with 51 claimed level scenes, inventory trades, snorkel/water hazards, thirty coins, boat assembly and taxman ending. Content map cites Spectrum/C64 walkthroughs; Godot gravity and collision implement new mechanics rather than proven recovered original algorithms.

Native 6809 implementation derived from released Fantasy World rules and data, alongside reusable differential-emulator tooling. Current port notes describe full tape/floppy routes, dialogue and thirty coins; the smaller run build has only 31 base rooms.
Native port of the winter Log Cabin mini-adventure using source supplied by BK author Sergey Shcherbakovsky. Assembly adapts display access and title RLE handling to UKNC hardware.

Game-specific demake of the PC DizzyAGE adventure, containing hotel rooms, dialogue, item identifiers and event/puzzle scripts. This is a different fan adventure, not a commercial Dizzy-series decompilation.

DizzyAGE-derived native engine replaces scripting integration with SWI-Prolog. C++ player accessors and material/collision predicates expose actual engine state to Prolog, beyond a README-only proposal.

Design documentation and multi-platform build skeleton are present, but game/game.cpp only displays a title and waits for VBlank (or immediately returns on desktop). No Kwik Snax gameplay implemented at this revision.
Source is the GBA Hello World template, not a reconstructed Dizzy game.

Treasure Island-labelled Canvas demo has four simple treasures, procedural scenery and a collect-all win condition; inventory and multiple levels are future work. It does not reconstruct the original puzzle adventure. Explicit AI authorship does not change this scope finding.

Construct 2 runtime export and packaged event/assets are present, but no original project source or evidence of original-game algorithm recovery established. Keep as a fan-demo lead rather than count a completed reconstruction.
Seven-file animation/experiment sandbox, not a recovered full Dizzy game.
Only a short Wonderful Dizzy cheat POK file and README; insufficient standalone reconstruction/analysis project.

Learning collection bundles DizzyAGE 2.4 engine/editor source and fan-game examples. Original Simion authorship is preserved in bundled documentation; do not promote this mirror as an independent reconstruction or confuse it with commercial Dizzy source.
Author identifies a prototype of their own Dizzy game using official graphics, not a reconstruction of a specified original adventure. Source tree has custom action classes.
PSP adaptation of the same author-created fan prototype; reused official artwork is not recovered original mechanics. No separate original-game reconstruction identity established.
Qt Windows adaptation of the same fan prototype, with documented screen judder/no vertical synchronization; not an independently recovered Dizzy title.
Linux Qt 5 adaptation of the same fan prototype. Do not multiply project counts for equivalent platform forks lacking a recovered original-game basis.
Small authoring tutorial collection, including dragon/climbing/jetpack examples, not a specific game reconstruction. Relevant support material but outside this game-first addition batch.
Generic WebGL 2D renderer; Dizzy name is a keyword collision, no connection to the Oliver Twins game series established.
Food recipes, not the Codemasters game; exact-name keyword collision.

classification.narrative: Native 6809 implementation derived from released Fantasy World rules and data, alongside reusable differential-emulator tooling. Current port notes describe full tape/floppy routes, dialogue and thirty coins; the smaller run build has only 31 base rooms.

build.narrative: Requires supplied pinned D3 sources and CoCo ROMs plus lwtools, Rust, Python and emulator tools. Author reports reproducible builds and route bots; no independent runs. Later port notes supersede the root README room-93 blocker but retain taller kill boxes, actor-clock timer differences, different randomness, silent heart sequence and untested physical hardware.
build.limitations: Source inspection only; no upstream game, installer, emulator, assembler or asset pipeline was run.

runtime_profiles.narrative: 64 KiB CoCo 2; floppy requires RS-DOS. Tape omits some negative-x scenery, floppy clips it; floppy joystick is not separately verified.

ai.narrative: README describes the actual end-to-end agent-driven port workflow and completed reference example, not just a speculative AI plan.

relationships.narrative: Use one repository-root record for its reference game and supporting factory. Original media are absent and generated locally. Cross-platform reproducibility means matching this port build, not identical Spectrum machine code.
